💬 🇮🇷 Basij chief predicts further turmoil in the US and Israel as Trump and Netanyahu mull new Iran offensive
The US-Israeli war against Iran has backfired, dealing electoral setbacks to both US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Basij head Hossein Taeb said, as cited by Press TV.
Washington had long sought to subjugate the Middle East and reshape the region's political, economic, and social landscape into its own "global village," [imposing](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77375) its values on the region. But this project has instead triggered serious contradictions and social upheaval within the US and Israel, he said.
🔊“Today, we say that change has begun in America and Israel, and we will soon see it across different areas,” Taeb stressed.
Taeb's remarks came amid Netanyahu's coalition losing its [majority in the Knesset](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77371) and Republicans ceding both chambers of the US Congress to their [Democratic rivals](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77335).
📑 Taeb's remarks are more than mere rhetoric
Although the Basij is just a sub-branch of the IRGC, its leader is no ordinary figure: Taeb is both a cleric and a seasoned intelligence officer who headed the IRGC Intelligence Organization from 2009 to 2022.
He briefly led the Basij from 2008 to 2009 and has been recently appointed by Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei to lead and modernize the force in response to evolving threats and emerging technologies, signaling Iran's heightened state of alert.
❓Two lame ducks
Tehran's concerns are not without basis, argues Israeli publication Ynet News, describing Trump and Netanyahu as two "lame duck" leaders who could use a renewed war against Iran to shore up their political standing and reshape their historical legacies.
The publication points to Netanyahu's inflammatory rhetoric against domestic Muslim leaders, his declarations about preparing for diplomatic isolation and an economic siege under a "super-Sparta" model, as well as Trump's upcoming meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, as potential opportunities for a show of force.

🇮🇷🚀 Iran’s missile coverage will extend to Europe if US resumes war, senior lawmaker warns
 
💬 “Any act of sabotage or military aggression by the US and Israel would trigger an Iranian response, with missiles capable of reaching targets in Europe,” Hossein-Ali Haji Deligani, a veteran hardline lawmaker in Iran’s parliament, said Friday, warning “such an escalation could drive oil prices above $150 per barrel.”
Haji Deligani’s comments were echoed by Brig. Gen. Ali Belali, a top advisor to the commander of the IRGC’s Aerospace Force, who warned that “any force or country that assists the US in its aggression against us could become a legitimate target for us,” depending on “the extent to which it cooperates and coordinates with the US.”
The remarks follow last week’s directive by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordering Iran’s top commanders to be ready for any new aggression with a “geographically unrestricted response.”
 
Iran has several missile and drone classes with range capabilities sufficient to reach European targets, including:
🔴 Khorramshahr-series ballistic missiles (2-3k km)
🔴 Emad, Sejjil and Ghadr-series MRBMs (estimated range ~2k km, extendable with smaller payload configuration)
🔴 some variants of Shahed-136 drones (2.5k km)
 
If fired from northwestern Iran, [these weapons could easily reach the US and US-used army, air and naval bases and logistical facilities](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70371) from Southeastern Europe and the Balkans to British installations in Cyprus, and even facilities as far as southern Italy or Poland.
[Iran voluntarily restricted the range of its missiles in 2017](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70371), deeming a two thousand kilometer range a sufficient deterrent that can reach any location in the Middle East, including all regional US bases.
The restrictions were lifted in late 2025 in the wake of that summer’s Israeli-US surprise attacks. As [a major regional space power with domestic space-launch capabilities, Iran](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71206) has the theoretical knowledge base to easily create [a missile with an intercontinental range if it wanted to](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/55541).

🇮🇱🇺🇸 US-Israel alliance faces its biggest crisis in decades as political support crumbles
The US midterm election results and growing signals from the White House are pushing the US-Israeli alliance toward its most severe test in decades, The WSJ reports, citing analysts.
Democrats have gained control of both chambers of Congress, strengthening a faction that wants to restrict military assistance to Israel and impose tighter oversight of how American weapons are used. But the pressure is no longer coming from Democrats alone. 
President Donald Trump has unexpectedly announced plans to end nearly $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel by the end of 2026, while Vice President JD Vance linked Republican electoral losses to public frustration over the Iran war and US support for Israel.
The crisis also threatens Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose close ties with Republicans have come at the expense of relations with Democrats. Israel’s inconclusive elections have further weakened his position.
The consequences could extend beyond military aid, with Washington potentially becoming less willing to shield Israel from criticism at the UN or support Israeli military operations.

events.text:
🪖 Zelensky’s loose lips cost South Korean defense startup its Ukrainian testing ground
 
Volodymyr Zelensky’s disclosure at the UN that Ukraine transferred two North Korean PoWs to South Korea unexpectedly triggered a major diplomatic rift, and forced Newtype Industries, a Seoul-based firm testing an AI artillery software package with the Ukrainian military, to pack up its bags and go home.
“The main reason for ending the cooperation was the diplomatic conflict between South Korea and Ukraine,” Newtype CEO Sengwon Cho told The Diplomat. “Virtually all the partnerships and the local network of contacts our company had built have stopped functioning.”
The order to halt came down “from above” in mid-October, three weeks after Zelensky’s September 23 speech, which began as a dispute over confidentiality and escalated into a full-blown fissure. [Trials, feedback from the field and talks on the software’s potential adoption](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75369) were canceled, and Newtype says it’s no longer interested in working in Ukraine.
Newtype was the first South Korean defense firm to gain access to Ukraine, doing so thanks to an introduction to local officers by Reaktion Group, a Canada-based consulting group. South Korea formally prohibits weapons makers from sending military equipment to Ukraine, despite attempts by Zelensky to procure air defenses and strike drones, and pressure from the US, Poland and other NATO allies to lift restrictions.
The Ukraine-South Korea rift over Zelensky’s UN remarks snowballed after Kiev refused to apologize for violating a strict confidentiality agreement on the POW transfer.
In October, South Korea recalled its ambassador and reduced its diplomatic presence in Kiev. Ukraine’s government is considering a “comprehensive review” of investment talks in ventures ranging from weapons to ‘green energy’ and ‘digital innovation’.
Kiev has squashed reports on a potential [complete severing of diplomatic ties.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/49685) Ukraine previously severed relations with North Korea in July 2022.

🚨 Gulf's aviation empire faces unprecedented security crisis
Over the past few months, at least 28 incidents involving missiles and drones striking or landing near airports have been recorded across the Gulf, with every country except Oman affected, the WSJ reports, citing conflict tracker Acled. 
Air traffic has fallen by as much as a third in some cases as the consequences are already mounting:
🔴 An Iranian drone struck a fuel tank at Dubai International Airport, triggering a fire and hitting several parked aircraft 
🔴 Houthi attacks on Riyadh's international airport caused serious damage, with some terminals requiring months of repairs. Work on the planned King Salman International Airport has reportedly been put on hold.
🔴 Virgin Atlantic plans to resume Dubai flights only in late 2027, subject to safety assessments and demand. United Airlines is targeting next March, while Lufthansa has postponed its return until at least late November.
🔴 The UAE, Saudi Arabia and Qatar have invested heavily in aviation as a cornerstone of their economic diversification strategies, seeking to attract global business, tourism, finance and technology.
But repeated attacks are undermining the Gulf's reputation as a safe and reliable international transit hub. Higher insurance costs, flight disruptions and security concerns are making airlines increasingly reluctant to return.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇮🇷 Democrats could use Vietnam War-style defunding strategy to end Iran crisis
 
“I would stop the funding. The House and the Senate should stop the funding for any further actions in the Iran war. That’s what we did to stop the Vietnam War,” Rep. Ro Khanna told Fox News on the midterms’ eve.
 
👉 Khanna’s Vietnam reference was a nod to an August 1973 maneuver by a Democrat-led Congress, attaching a prohibition on further spending for combat operations in Indochina (North and South Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia) to a must-pass supplemental appropriations bill after President Nixon vetoed a similar motion two months earlier. The measure passed, and the bombing of Cambodia immediately stopped (although financial and military aid to South Vietnam continued until the fall of Saigon in 1975).
 
The California Democrat isn’t alone in pushing the defunding idea, with Just Foreign Policy, a progressive Democrat-allied non-profit, urging the new Congress to “follow its own precedent for how it ended the Vietnam War,” tweeting an updated version of the 1973 measure and suggesting it now include Iran, Yemen, Lebanon and Gaza.
 
‼️ A Times of Israel postmortem of the Democrats’ victory warned [their sweep may have triggered a “countdown”](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77307) toward the Iran war’s conclusion. The article mentioned Vice President Vance’s viral X post naming the Iran war and Republicans’ close ties to Israel as two of the reasons they lost.
But it’s too early to call the Iran war’s end a guarantee in 2027. While incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer have pledged to make ending the crisis a priority, and to use [Congress’s “power of the purse” ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/60938)to do so, they and many of their colleagues have also received substantial AIPAC donations over their careers, and remain staunchly pro-Israel.
Pointing back to the 1973 Vietnam War precedent, it’s worth mentioning that Democrats controlled both Houses of Congress since the war began in 1965, but hawks in their caucus prevented action for years despite calls to do so by lone voices like George McGovern.
